conventions.convention: Fields are smooth sections of a smooth bundle over a four-manifold. Variations are derivatives of jointly smooth finite-dimensional parameter families; commuting coordinate variations are used for component calculations.
The first variation is δL = E[δφ] + d_Mθ. The current is ω = −d_PΘ, hence ω(δ1,δ2) = δ2θ(δ1) − δ1θ(δ2). Parameter derivatives of Euler coefficients hold the variation input fixed.
Integration uses fixed finite oriented smooth singular three-chains. No infinite-chain convergence, asymptotic limit, or global infinite-dimensional field manifold is assumed.
The boundary decomposition is ∂C = Σ2 − Σ1 + B, so the cut difference equals minus the oriented side flux.

A reduction requires a specified smooth Hausdorff quotient, a surjective submersion with connected fibers and kernel equal to ker Ω, and a supplied descended closed nondegenerate form. Hamiltonians satisfy ι_XΩ = dH.

Surface-charge integrability means global exactness of α_ξ(v) = Ω(X_ξ,v). The generator comes from a specified smooth lifted action preserving the solution manifold and boundary conditions. Closedness on a star-shaped parameter chart supplies only a local primitive.
The scalar examples use signature (−,+,+,+), orientation dt∧dx∧dy∧dz, and *dt = −dx∧dy∧dz. Constant-time cuts have orientation dx∧dy∧dz; side orientations are outward-normal-first.

load_bearing.statement: A chosen smooth finite-order local first-variation decomposition satisfies δL = E_φ[δφ] + d_Mθ(φ;δφ). On each smooth finite-dimensional field family, Θ_p(v) = θ(φ_p;δ_vφ_p), ω := −d_PΘ, and Ω_Σ := ∫_Σω for a finite oriented smooth singular three-chain.
A smooth field family is a smooth map Φ:P×M→E with π(Φ(p,x))=x, where P is finite-dimensional. Its variation along u∈T_pP is the derivative along a parameter curve with initial velocity u.
For a smooth two-parameter family with commuting variations, d_Mω(δ1φ,δ2φ) = (δ1E_φ)[δ2φ] − (δ2E_φ)[δ1φ], using the chosen first-variation decomposition and current ordering.

At E_φ=0, if each commuting variation satisfies (δ_iE_φ)[η]=0 for every smooth test variation with input held fixed, then d_Mω=0. For a finite oriented smooth singular four-chain with ∂C=Σ2−Σ1+B, Ω_Σ2−Ω_Σ1=−∫_Bω.
For an open U⊆R^n star-shaped about a and a smooth closed k-form α with 1≤k≤n, the stated radial integral Kα is smooth and satisfies d(Kα)=α.

For a fixed finite oriented smooth singular three-chain and a smooth parameter-dependent three-form with jointly smooth simplex pullback coefficients, I(p)=∫_Σα_p is smooth and d_PI_p(v)=∫_Σd_Pα_p(v).

Under L′=L+d_Mμ and θ′=θ+δμ+d_MY, with the stated smooth finite-order locality and variation-linearity hypotheses, ω′−ω=d_M(δ2Y(δ1φ)−δ1Y(δ2φ)). Its integral over a finite three-chain is the corresponding boundary integral.

For a smooth finite-dimensional field family and every finite oriented smooth singular three-chain Σ, Ω_Σ=∫_Σ(−d_PΘ) satisfies d_PΩ_Σ=0 without equations of motion; its restriction to a smooth solution family is also closed.
